standards.title: Never enter from scale(0)
standards.rule: Never animate an element in from scale(0) or out to scale(0); start from scale(0.9–0.97) together with opacity: 0, and use scale(0.95) + opacity: 0 as the replacement.
standards.why: scale(0) looks like the element comes out of nowhere; nothing in the real world appears from nothing (or disappears and reappears completely), and a higher start scale is like a balloon, which keeps a visible shape even when deflated.

standards.title: Ease-out for entrances and exits
standards.rule: Use ease-out, as the strong curve cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), for every element entering or exiting; never use ease-in on any UI element, and do not put bare ease or linear on an entrance. The one sourced exception is the web toast recipe (Sonner), which uses ease at 400ms to match the component's personality; the React Native toast recipe keeps the ease-out curve.
standards.why: Ease-out starts fast, which feels responsive; ease-in starts slow and delays the exact moment the user is watching, so a 300ms ease-in dropdown feels slower than a 300ms ease-out one. Built-in CSS easings are too weak.

standards.rule: Make an element leave along the same path and edge it entered from: a toast or panel that slides in from the bottom or right dismisses to the bottom or right. standards.rule: When an element slides fully in or out by its own size (a toast, drawer or sheet), express the distance as a percentage of that size, such as translateY(100%), rather than a hardcoded pixel offset. standards.title: React Native: never animate header height

standards.title: Scroll reveals on marketing pages only
standards.rule: Use scroll-triggered reveals only on marketing surfaces, never on functional UI a user visits daily.
standards.why: The recipe limits scroll reveals to marketing surfaces; a surface visited daily falls under the frequency gate, where repeated motion makes the interface feel slow, and data the user reads or acts on should not move for style.

sources.evidence: Scroll reveal: 'Marketing surfaces only. Don't do this to functional UI a user visits daily.'
4. Function: 'Data the user is trying to read or act on should not move for style.'

standards.title: Fire scroll reveals once, 100px in
standards.rule: Trigger a scroll reveal when the element enters the viewport and fire it only once (IntersectionObserver, or Motion's useInView with { once: true, margin: "-100px" }, which fires once at least 100px of the element is in view).
standards.why: The reveal must run where the user can see it, or they never see it animate; re-animating on every scroll-by is an interface fighting its reader.

sources.evidence: Scroll reveal: 'useInView with { once: true, margin: "-100px" }. Fire it once'
Scroll animations: 'The image reveal effect must be triggered when the image enters the viewport'; 'triggered only once' and 'when at least 100px of the image is in view'

standards.title: Blur a crossfade that won't settle
standards.rule: When a crossfade still shows two overlapping states after you have tried other easings and durations, add filter: blur(2px) during the transition (recipe: opacity 0.7, filter and opacity over 200ms ease).
standards.why: Without blur the eye reads two distinct objects swapping; blur blends them into one perceived transformation.

standards.title: Keep animated blur under 20px
standards.rule: Keep any animated or transition-time blur() under 20px.
standards.why: Heavy blur is expensive, especially in Safari, and causes performance issues.

standards.title: Materialize glass surfaces, don't fade
standards.rule: When a glass or blurred surface enters or exits, animate its blur radius and scale together rather than using a plain opacity fade.
standards.why: The surface then reads as a real material arriving rather than a plain opacity fade.

sources.evidence: Materials: 'Materialize, don't just fade.'

standards.title: React Native: never animate BlurView
standards.rule: In React Native, never animate BlurView intensity; crossfade the opacity of a static BlurView instead.
standards.why: On Android, animating intensity re-renders the blur every frame.

sources.evidence: 'Never animate BlurView intensity. On Android it re-renders the blur each frame.'

review.message: Don't animate BlurView intensity: crossfade the opacity of a static BlurView.

standards.title: No entering on virtualized rows
standards.rule: Never put an entering animation on a row inside FlatList, FlashList or any virtualized list; animate the list container once on mount, or use itemLayoutAnimation for reflow only.
standards.why: Rows are recycled, so the animation re-fires every time one scrolls back into view and the list appears to flicker while the user scrolls.

sources.evidence: List entrances: 'Never put entering on a row inside FlatList, FlashList, or any virtualized list.'
Never Ship: 'entering on a virtualized list row | animate the container, or itemLayoutAnimation'

review.message: No entering on virtualized list rows: animate the container once, or use itemLayoutAnimation for reflow.

standards.title: The list closes a removed row's gap
standards.rule: When a row is removed, let the list close the gap with itemLayoutAnimation={LinearTransition.duration(200)}, the builder defined at module scope, rather than animating the row.
standards.why: Closing the gap the deleted row left is the list's job, not the row's.

sources.evidence: Swipe to delete: 'Closing the gap the deleted row left is the list's job, not the row's'; ROW_CLOSE = LinearTransition.duration(200)

standards.title: Layout animations for mount and unmount
standards.rule: In React Native, animate elements mounting or unmounting and lists reflowing with Reanimated layout animations (entering, exiting, itemLayoutAnimation).
standards.why: The animate-expo tool table, walked from the top to the cheapest tool that fits, assigns mounting, unmounting and list reflow to layout animations.

sources.evidence: tool table: 'An element mounting or unmounting, or a list reflowing | Layout animations'

standards.title: Build layout-animation builders once
standards.rule: Define Reanimated layout-animation builders at module scope or in useMemo, never inline in JSX; a per-index delay is memoized inside the row.
standards.why: The Reanimated docs recommend building layout animations outside components or in useMemo, because an inline builder chain in JSX rebuilds the builder on every render.

sources.evidence: List entrances: 'The Reanimated docs recommend building layout animations outside components, or in useMemo'; Toast: 'Module scope — layout-animation builders live outside the component.'

standards.title: Tune opacity against height by eye
standards.rule: When items enter or exit a list with a height change (including reflowing toast stacks), tune the opacity change against the height animation by eye and check it again the next day.
standards.why: The opacity change has to work with the height change and there is no formula for that pair; imperfections show up with fresh eyes.

sources.evidence: The opacity + height combination: 'There is no formula'

standards.title: Set every transform-origin on purpose
standards.rule: Check the transform-origin of every scaled or rotated element, SVG elements included, and set it to where the motion should grow from instead of relying on the default; verify it in slow motion.
standards.why: Every element transforms from an anchor point whose default is center, and slow-motion review checks whether an element scales from the wrong point.

sources.evidence: transform-origin: 'Every element has an anchor point ... The default is center.'; slow motion: 'Is the transform-origin correct'

standards.title: Mirror easing on reversible transitions
standards.rule: On a reversible transition, mirror the easing so the outbound path matches the return path (inverse cubic-bézier control points for the two directions); for UI entrances and exits the ease-out rule (STD-enter-exit-origin-05) still applies, since the inverse of an ease-out is an ease-in [inferred].
standards.why: Apple: if something disappears one way, we expect it to emerge from where it came.

sources.evidence: 7. Spatial consistency: 'Mirror the easing on reversible transitions'

standards.title: Vaul: --initial-transform off the edge
standards.rule: When a Vaul side drawer does not touch the screen edge, adjust its enter and exit animation with the --initial-transform CSS variable.
standards.why: The Vaul docs name --initial-transform as the way to adjust the animation when the drawer does not touch the edge. Vaul is good-to-have only: its README says the library is unmaintained (learn/sources.json, checked 2026-09-24).

sources.evidence: Side drawer: 'Use the --initial-transform CSS variable to adjust the animation'

standards.title: Drawers: 500ms on the drawer curve
standards.rule: Hide a drawer or sheet at transform: translateY(100%) and open and close it with transition: transform 500ms var(--ease-drawer), where --ease-drawer is cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1); once a drag is involved it becomes a gesture and settles with a spring instead.
standards.why: The curve closely matches iOS (it comes from the Ionic Framework) and 500ms is meant to mimic iOS's sheet; translateY(100%) hides the drawer by its own height whatever its content, which is how Vaul hides a drawer before animating it in.

sources.evidence: Drawer / sheet: 'transition: transform 500ms var(--ease-drawer)'; '.drawer[data-closed] { transform: translateY(100%) }'; 'This is how Vaul hides a drawer before animating it in.'
Motion: 'The curve used in Vaul closely matches the one used in iOS'; 'Duration of 500ms is also supposed to mimic iOS's Sheet'

standards.title: Web toasts: 400ms ease from below
standards.rule: On the web, enter a toast from opacity: 0 and transform: translateY(100%) to its resting position with transition: opacity 400ms ease, transform 400ms ease, set through @starting-style (or a mounted flag set in useEffect where @starting-style is unavailable).
standards.why: A toast that suddenly appears would feel off; ease at 400ms, slightly slower than typical UI, is tuned to Sonner's personality and is part of why it reads as elegant, and translateY(100%) moves the toast by its own height whatever its content.

sources.evidence: Toast: 'transition: opacity 400ms ease, transform 400ms ease; @starting-style { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(100%); }'; 'ease rather than ease-out, slightly slower than typical UI'
